tools.name: convertapi_get_account
tools.description: Show the ConvertAPI account status and conversion quota: Active, Status, ConversionsTotal, ConversionsConsumed, ConversionsLeft. Call this first to check quota before converting. Never returns the account secret. ConvertAPI: GET /user.

tools.name: convertapi_get_usage_statistics
tools.description: Show conversions per day between two dates for this account, as JSON. Use it to report usage over a period. ConvertAPI: GET /user/statistic?startDate&endDate.

tools.name: convertapi_get_converter
tools.description: Describe one conversion, for example pdf to docx: its title, the accepted source and destination formats, and the parameter names and types it takes. Read it before convert_file so the parameters are right. ConvertAPI: GET /info/openapi (catalog, filtered to one path).

tools.name: convertapi_convert_file
tools.description: Convert a file from one format to another. The file must be at a public https URL that ConvertAPI can read; local files cannot be sent. Each successful conversion costs ConversionCost conversions from the account quota. Returns download URLs that stay valid for a few hours. ConvertAPI: POST /convert

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "convertapi_get_account" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Show the ConvertAPI account status and conversion quota: Active, Status, ConversionsTotal, ConversionsConsumed, ConversionsLeft. Call this first to check quota …

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: convertapi_convert_file · Private data: convertapi_get_account, convertapi_convert_file · Public sink: convertapi_convert_file · Destructive: convertapi_convert_file.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: convertapi_convert_file · Private data: convertapi_get_account, convertapi_convert_file · Public sink: convertapi_convert_file · Destructive: convertapi_convert_file

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
